Article Title: 'Shan Masood's injury affected us': Pakistan captain Babar Azam after 1st Test defeat to West Indies
Article Text:
Pakistan's Babar Azam (Photo by AP)

Babar rues batting collapse

Greaves shines for West Indies

Pakistan captain Babar Azam has revealed that Shan Masood fractured his finger during the first Test against the West Indies in Trinidad, an injury that affected the team's batting plans in their 90-run defeat.Masood picked up the injury while batting in the first innings and was forced to bat at No. 8 in the second innings. Pakistan were bowled out for just 120 as they slumped to their eighth straight away Test defeat, leaving them at the bottom of the ICC World Test Championship standings."Yes, Shan Masood's injury affected us because, unfortunately, his finger is fractured, so we definitely missed him," Babar confirmed.He added, "At the same time, when you're facing the new ball, you have to survive the first 20 overs, build partnerships, and then, as the ball gets older, the pitch becomes easier to bat on. We couldn't put together those partnerships."Babar scored a fighting half-century, but Pakistan's batting line-up failed to support him as Jayden Seales claimed five wickets."We played good cricket in the last few days, but today we were not up to the mark as a batting unit," Babar said."The surface is good and we expected the new ball to move for which we were prepared ... but I think they bowled very well and used the conditions nicely. We'll sit together and discuss these things because, while the result isn't go our way, we can certainly address our mistakes. We'll do our best to correct them and ensure we improve going forward," he added.Justin Greaves was named Player of the Match after taking his maiden five-wicket haul in the first innings before adding two more wickets in the second.He said, "We came in and tried to be just as disciplined as possible. I mimicked Mohammad Abbas' fuller lengths when he bowled against us in the first and second innings and it pretty much worked out for us."The second Test begins in Port of Spain on August 2.
Article Summary: Pakistan captain Babar Azam reveals that Shan Masood fractured his finger during the first Test against the West Indies. Masood picked up the injury while batting in the first innings and was forced to bat at No. 8 in the second innings. Pakistan were bowled out for just 120 as they slumped to their eighth straight away Test defeat. The second Test begins in Port of Spain on August 2.

Article Title: Who is Subhadeep Ghosh? Meet Team India's new fielding coach after T Dilip's exit
Article Text:
Subhadeep Ghosh (Image credit: X)

Who is Subhadeep Ghosh ?

NEW DELHI: Team India will have a new face in its support staff as Subhadeep Ghosh takes over as the fielding coach, replacing T Dilip. The BCCI has decided against extending Dilip's contract after it ended following India's white-ball tour of England.Subhadeep's first assignment with the senior men's team will be India's two-Test series in Sri Lanka in August.Subhadeep Ghosh, who has been appointed as India's new fielding coach after Dilip's tenure came to an end, is a former domestic cricketer from Assam. Born in Digboi, Assam, in 1968, he played as a middle-order right-handed batter and an off-spinner.During his playing career, he represented Assam and Railways in domestic cricket.Ghosh featured in 17 First-Class matches and 17 List A games, scoring 316 and 307 runs respectively. He made his debut in both formats during the 1994-95 season.He played his last First-Class match in 2004 and ended his List A career in 2005.After retiring as a player, Ghosh moved into coaching and became part of India's cricket development structure.He has been associated with the National Cricket Academy (NCA) for the last six to seven years and worked during Rahul Dravid's time at the NCA.Over the years, Ghosh has gained experience by working with various Indian teams across different age groups.Ghosh served as the fielding coach of the Indian women's team during their tour of Australia in 2021.He has also worked with India A and the India Under-19 team, including during the 2024 Under-19 World Cup campaign in South Africa.In the IPL, Ghosh was part of the Kolkata Knight Riders support staff in 2014, when the franchise won its second title.He later worked as the fielding coach of Delhi Capitals.
Article Summary: Subhadeep Ghosh replaces T Dilip as India's new fielding coach. Ghosh is a former domestic cricketer from Assam. He played as a middle-order right-handed batter and an off-spinner. His first assignment with the senior men's team will be in Sri Lanka in August.

Article Title: 'We can't write his obituary immediately': R Ashwin on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (AFP Photo)

Ashwin clears the air



Sooryavanshi returns to form against Zimbabwe



'We can't write his obituary immediately'



Former India spinner Ravichandran Ashwin has cleared the air over his "serve drinks" remark about young batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Ashwin said the comment was not made in a negative way and his intention was to highlight the importance of learning for the 15-year-old by spending time around the team.Ashwin had earlier said that Sooryavanshi could "serve drinks" or sit out if he was not picked in the playing XI.However, the former spinner explained that his words were misunderstood.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin said: “I had said earlier that Vaibhav Sooryavanshi ‘can spend time, can serve someone drinks, can sit outside.' It was not in a derogatory manner."Explaining his point, he added, “I was saying that he will get so much to learn. He has such a huge learning curve to go through that if he observes it while sitting outside, he'll become even better. Don't talk about dropping or picking - let him be, let him evolve. He'll be a really phenomenal player."Sooryavanshi made his international debut during India's T20I series against England but failed to make a big impact. The teenager scored 14, 13 and 15 in the three matches he played.The youngster, however, quickly bounced back in the T20I series against Zimbabwe.He scored a half-century in the opening match, followed it with a 20-run knock and then smashed a brilliant 81 in the final game.The left-hander finished the series with 151 runs from three matches at an average of 50.33 and an impressive strike rate of 196.10. His performances earned him the Player of the Series award.Ashwin also spoke about Sooryavanshi's struggles against England fast bowler Jofra Archer, who dismissed him with short deliveries during the T20I series in England.“Who do you think is the strongest batsman against the short ball? Ricky Ponting? Did he never get out on a short ball? He got out too. So we have to understand everyone has strengths, everyone has weaknesses. These things are common in international cricket. It's simple — show your strengths, hide your weaknesses, and keep working on them behind the scenes. All these questions… How many times did he play against Jofra Archer at Trent Bridge? These are all experiences. We can't write his obituary immediately. Can't write someone off just like that," Ashwin said.Ashwin also pointed out that Sooryavanshi's strong IPL performances have increased expectations around him.“He's such a young kid. The problem is, we rate him so highly; he performed so well in the IPL, expectations skyrocketed. We expect him to perform like Virat Kohli or Rohit Sharma every match, to be consistent. That's not how it works. There will be ups and downs in life, in cricket too," he said.
Article Summary: Ravichandran Ashwin has cleared the air over his'serve drinks' remark about Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. Ashwin said the comment was not made in a negative way and his intention was to highlight the importance of learning for the 15-year-old by spending time around the team. The former spinner explained that his words were misunderstood.

Article Title: Jayden Seales' five-for powers West Indies to 90-run win over Pakistan in first Test
Article Text:
AFP Photo

Babar stands tall in defeat



Pakistan suffer another batting collapse



West Indies build a match-winning lead



Seales and Greaves lead West Indies attack



West Indies took a 1-0 lead in the two-match Test series after defeating Pakistan by 90 runs in the opening match of the two-match series at the Brian Lara Stadium in Trinidad. Fast bowler Jayden Seales was the star performer, claiming five wickets in the second innings as Pakistan were bowled out for 120 while chasing 211.Seales finished with figures of 5/20.Pakistan's batting collapsed quickly as they slipped to 71/9. However, captain Babar Azam and No. 11 Mohammad Abbas delayed the West Indies victory with a 49-run partnership for the final wicket.Abbas scored 23 before Seales dismissed him shortly after the tea break on Day 4, bringing an end to Pakistan's fight.Babar Azam remained unbeaten on 58 and completed his 32nd Test half-century, but the Pakistan captain received little support from his teammates.Babar reached his fifty from 81 balls when Pakistan were already struggling at 88/9. The other batters had managed only 38 runs between them.After the defeat, Babar admitted Pakistan's batting was not good enough.“We played good cricket in the last few days but today we were not up to the mark as a batting unit. We lost back-to-back wickets. We will look to make sure it doesn’t happen in the next matches,” Babar said.The second Test of the series will begin on Sunday.Pakistan's second innings defeat reflected their first innings problems.After reaching 244/4, Pakistan lost six wickets for just 38 runs and were dismissed for 282, handing West Indies a 29-run first-innings lead.West Indies had posted 311 in their first innings.Apart from Shan Masood 's century and half-centuries from Imam-ul-Haq (63) and Babar Azam, Pakistan's batting lacked consistency. Across both innings, only six Pakistan batters managed to score in double figures.Masood's injury made things more difficult for Pakistan. After hurting his hand in the first innings, he was forced to bat at No. 8 instead of his usual No. 3 position.West Indies resumed Day 4 at 126/7 with a lead of 155 runs. Shamar Joseph added 16 runs to his overnight score of 22, while Kemar Roach contributed 13 as West Indies pushed their advantage beyond 200.The target proved too much for Pakistan as Imam-ul-Haq was dismissed for just three runs early in the chase.Babar tried to anchor the innings, but the rest of the batting line-up failed to provide support. Among Pakistan's top six, only Mohammad Rizwan crossed double figures with a score of 11.Seales received good support from Kemar Roach and Justin Greaves, who picked up two wickets each.The pacer completed his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket when he trapped Abbas lbw in the 41st over.Greaves was named Player of the Match after his impressive performance. He had taken 5/27 in Pakistan's first innings.For Pakistan, Abbas was the standout performer with the ball, taking 3/63 and 5/22 in the two West Indies innings.
Article Summary: West Indies beat Pakistan by 90 runs in the opening Test of the series. Fast bowler Jayden Seales took five wickets as Pakistan were bowled out for 120. Pakistan's batting collapsed quickly as they slipped to 71/9. West Indies took a 1-0 lead in the two-match Test series.

Article Title: India opener Pratika Rawal set for County Cricket debut, joins Warwickshire for One-Day Cup
Article Text:
Pratika Rawal signs Warwickshire

Return after injury

A rapid rise in international cricket

India batter Pratika Rawal has signed with Warwickshire Women for the remainder of the 2026 domestic season, with the 25-year-old set to strengthen the county side's batting line-up in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup. Rawal will be available for selection from Warwickshire's next One-Day Cup fixture on August 19, as the Bears continue their push for a place in the tournament's eliminators.The move marks Rawal's return to competitive cricket after recovering from a knee injury that ruled her out of India's one-off Test against England at Lord's. She suffered the injury during an India A match in Taunton on July 1, requiring stitches and forcing her to miss the landmark Test.Warwickshire currently occupy fifth place in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup standings and are aiming to finish inside the top three to qualify for the knockout stage. The club believes Rawal's arrival will provide added firepower at the top of the order during the closing stages of the competition.Welcoming the India opener, the club said her addition would strengthen the squad as they look to finish the season strongly."It's a great signing for the team, and we are most pleased to be able to welcome Pratika to Edgbaston. Our position in the One Day Cup table at the moment is a good one, and bringing in a player of Pratika's calibre can only serve to strengthen our team as we aim to end the season on a positive note," the club said in a statement.Rawal said she is eager to experience county cricket and is looking forward to representing Warwickshire at one of England's most iconic venues."I am most pleased to be joining Warwickshire; I have heard many positive things about the club and am excited to get going and do all I can to assist the team. Testing myself by playing in England will be a great experience for me, and I'm also looking forward to walking out at Edgbaston, which is such an iconic ground in world cricket," she said.Rawal has emerged as one of India's brightest batting talents since making her international debut in December 2024. She holds the record as the fastest woman to reach 500 ODI runs, achieving the milestone in just eight innings. The opener also played a key role in India's successful Women's ODI World Cup campaign, scoring 308 runs, including a century against New Zealand, to help the team lift the title in 2025.
Article Summary: Pratika Rawal signs with Warwickshire Women for remainder of 2026 domestic season. The 25-year-old is set to strengthen the county side's batting line-up in the Metro Bank One-Day Cup. The move marks Rawal's return to competitive cricket after recovering from a knee injury that ruled her out of India's one- off Test against England.

Article Title: English cricket club under fire after 'Clicky Ponting' finger-click cheating claim goes viral
Article Text:
Finger click sparked a cheating scandal (Image: BBC/X)

What happened?

More allegations surface

League launches investigation

An amateur cricket match in England has found itself at the centre of a major controversy after a fielder was accused of using a finger-clicking trick to fool the umpire into giving a batter out. The incident, which has gone viral on social media and is now being called "Clickgate" or "Clicky Ponting", occurred during a North Yorkshire and South Durham (NYSD) Cricket League Division Two match between Saltburn Cricket Club 2nd XI and Norton Cricket Club.The controversy revolves around a dismissal involving Norton batter Noman Shabir. As the bowler delivered the ball, it passed close to Shabir's bat without appearing to make contact. At that exact moment, a Saltburn fielder stationed at first slip clicked his fingers, creating a sharp sound that closely resembled the noise of the ball edging the bat. The wicketkeeper caught the ball cleanly, Saltburn's players immediately appealed, and the umpire, believing he had heard an edge, gave the batter out.Shabir protested the decision, insisting he had not touched the ball, but the umpire stood by his verdict.A video of the incident quickly spread across social media, with many viewers claiming the finger click had deliberately deceived the umpire.Saltburn won by 159 runs and are top of Division 2 by 18 points.The controversy did not stop with the viral video. Following the incident, cricket fans began analysing Saltburn's statistics and previous matches. One statistic that attracted attention was wicketkeeper Josh Bowes' tally of 31 catches in just eight matches, including eight catches in a single innings against Shildon Railway.For comparison, the world record for catches by a wicketkeeper in a men's Test innings is seven, making the figure unusual enough to fuel further speculation, although the statistic alone is not evidence of wrongdoing.Soon after, Rory Cotterill, captain of Middlesbrough Second XI, publicly claimed his side had experienced two similar finger-clicking incidents during a defeat to Saltburn earlier in the season. Another video from a separate match against Wolviston FC has also emerged online, showing a batter being dismissed under similar circumstances, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the club.The North Yorkshire and South Durham Cricket League confirmed it has received a formal complaint and has opened an investigation.In a statement, the league said: "The league have received a formal complaint regarding alleged incidents in a Division Two game on Saturday. A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made."The unusual incident has attracted worldwide attention. The original video has been viewed more than five million times on X (formerly Twitter), while cricket fans from around the world have debated whether the dismissal should stand.Former newspaper editor and television presenter Piers Morgan also reacted, describing the player involved as the "biggest cheat in cricket history", a comment that further amplified the controversy online.
Article Summary: Incident occurred during a North Yorkshire and South Durham (NYSD) Cricket League Division Two match between Saltburn Cricket Club 2nd XI and Norton Cricket Club. The controversy revolves around a dismissal involving Norton batter Noman Shabir. A Saltburn fielder stationed at first slip clicked his fingers, creating a sharp sound that closely resembled the noise of the ball edging the bat. The wicketkeeper caught the ball cleanly, and the umpire, believing he had heard an edge, gave the batter out.

Article Title: Ryan ten Doeschate steps down as India's assistant coach; Subhadeep Ghosh replaces T Dilip as fielding coach
Article Text:
Subhadeep Ghosh to be India's new fielding coach; Ten Doeschate quits, Dilip's contract not extended (Images: Agencies)

MUMBAI: Ryan ten Doeschate has stepped down as India's men's assistant coach, bringing an end to his two-year stint with the national team, while Subhadeep Ghosh will be India's new fielding coach after T Dilip's contract came to an end and was not renewed, TOI has learnt.Ten Doeschate and Dilip's final assignment was India's white-ball tour of England. Both will, thus, not travel with Team India for their two-Test tour of Sri Lanka in August, while it will be the first international assignment for Subhadeep, who has been the fielding coach of India A teams in the past.During India's England tour, Ten Doeschate informed the BCCI of his decision to leave, despite being offered an extension until 2027 by the board. Although the BCCI was keen to retain him, the former Netherlands all-rounder declined the offer, citing personal reasons. With a young family, Ten Doeschate opted to step away from the demands of international cricket and its relentless travel schedule.Meanwhile, fielding coach T Dilip is parting ways with the national team following the completion of his tenure. He will not travel with the squad for the upcoming Test tour of Sri Lanka.Ten Doeschate joined the Indian coaching setup in July 2024 after former India opener Gautam Gambhir succeeded Rahul Dravid as the head coach following India's T20 World Cup triumph. Having worked closely with Gambhir during their successful stint at Kolkata Knight Riders, the former Netherlands all-rounder was brought into the national setup by Gambhir alongside bowling coach Morne Morkel.During Ten Doeschate's stint, India won the Champions Trophy and the Asia Cup in 2025 and successfully defended the 2026 T20 World Cup, although the Test side endured a difficult period, losing the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in Australia before suffering series defeats against New Zealand (3-0) and South Africa (2-0) at home.
Article Summary: Subhadeep Ghosh will be India's new fielding coach. Ryan ten Doeschate has stepped down as India's men's assistant coach. T Dilip's contract came to an end and was not renewed. Both will not travel with Team India for their two-Test tour of Sri Lanka.

Article Title: Jai Moondra earns maiden call-up as Ireland announce injury-hit squad for Afghanistan ODIs
Article Text:
Jai Moondra .(Photo-X/Cricket Ireland)

Paul Stirling returns, injury list remains long

Ireland squad for first three ODIs against Afghanistan

Ireland have announced a 14-member squad for the first three ODIs of their five-match series against Afghanistan, beginning on August 5, with several first-choice players unavailable due to injuries. The selectors have opted to announce the squad only for the opening three matches, with the remaining two ODIs to be finalised after assessing the fitness of injured players.One of the biggest talking points is the inclusion of Jai Moondra, who made his T20I debut against India earlier this month and impressed during Ireland's historic T20I series triumph over the reigning world champions. The youngster has now received his maiden ODI call-up and is one of two capped T20I players in the squad, alongside Ben Calitz, yet to make their 50-over international debut.Ireland have also handed a first international call-up to medium pacer Byron McDonough. The 24-year-old enjoyed an impressive domestic campaign with Leinster Lightning, helping them win the Inter-Provincial Limited Overs Cup after claiming eight wickets in five matches. Across nine List A appearances, McDonough has picked up 15 wickets at an average of 29.33.Captain Paul Stirling returns to lead the side after missing the recent T20I series against India through injury.However, Ireland continue to deal with a lengthy injury list, with Josh Little, Matt Hollard, Craig Young, Barry McCarthy, Jordan Neill and David Delany all unavailable due to injuries or return-to-play protocols. Cricket Ireland confirmed that the squad for the final two ODIs will be announced later, with changes possible depending on the recovery of the injured players.The Afghanistan series will mark the first assignment for newly appointed head coach Gary Wilson, who recently replaced Heinrich Malan. Former England batter Jonathan Trott will also join the Irish camp as a consultant for the first two ODIs against Afghanistan, having previously served as the Afghan national team's head coach.The five-match series will also be Ireland's first men's bilateral ODI assignment since hosting the West Indies in May 2025. The opening two matches will be played in Bready, while the remaining three fixtures will take place at Stormont.Paul Stirling (captain), Mark Adair, Andrew Balbirnie, Ben Calitz, Curtis Campher, Cade Carmichael, George Dockrell, Gavin Hoey, Andrew McBrine, Liam McCarthy, Byron McDonough, Jai Moondra, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker.
Article Summary: Ireland have announced a 14-member squad for the first three ODIs of their five- match series against Afghanistan, beginning on August 5. The selectors have opted to announce the squad only for the opening three matches, with the remaining two ODIs to be finalised after assessing the fitness of injured players. Captain Paul Stirling returns to lead the side after missing the recent T20I series against India through injury.

Article Title: Sri Lanka women end 24-year wait, beat Pakistan 2-1 to clinch historic ODI series
Article Text:
Sri Lanka Women End 24-Year Wait, Beat Pakistan 2-1 to Clinch Historic ODI Series

Sri Lanka bounce back after opening defeat

Pakistan collapse after bright rebuild

Athapaththu leads comfortable chase

Sri Lanka Women produced a remarkable comeback to clinch their first bilateral ODI series victory over Pakistan Women in 24 years, sealing a 2-1 triumph with a dominant eight-wicket win in the series decider at Hambantota on Tuesday. After dropping the opening ODI, the hosts responded emphatically by chasing down a record target in the second match before delivering a clinical all-round performance in the third to end Pakistan's run of four consecutive ODI series wins over Sri Lanka. It was also Sri Lanka's first bilateral ODI series triumph over Pakistan since 2002.Pakistan had drawn first blood in the series with a five-wicket victory after restricting Sri Lanka to 210/9 in the opener. However, Sri Lanka responded in spectacular fashion in the second ODI, completing their highest successful run chase in women's ODIs. Vishmi Gunaratne smashed 123, while Harshitha Samarawickrama remained unbeaten on 100 as the hosts chased down 274 with eight wickets in hand to level the series.That momentum carried into the decider, where Sri Lanka outplayed Pakistan in every department to complete a memorable turnaround.Asked to bat first, Pakistan suffered a nightmare start as Chetana Vimukthi ripped through the top order in just the second over. The visitors slumped to 10/3, putting themselves under immediate pressure. Gull Feroza and Muneeba Ali steadied the innings with a 68-run partnership, but Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu broke the stand by dismissing Feroza for 40.Pakistan's middle order failed to capitalise as another collapse followed. From 110/4, the visitors slipped to 146/7 before captain Fatima Sana played a fighting knock of 41 to lift her side to 187 all out in 40 overs. Athapaththu and Kavisha Dilhari starred with the ball, claiming three wickets each to keep Pakistan below the 200-run mark.Needing 188 for victory, Sri Lanka lost Vishmi Gunaratne early after she had helped provide another positive start. Captain Chamari Athapaththu quickly seized control, attacking Pakistan's bowlers with trademark aggression. She struck three boundaries and a six in one over before bringing up the 30th fifty-plus score of her ODI career, ensuring Sri Lanka stayed comfortably ahead of the required rate.Although Athapaththu departed after scoring 52, Harshitha Samarawickrama continued her excellent form, remaining unbeaten on 71, while Hasini Perera provided steady support in an unbroken partnership that guided Sri Lanka home with 76 balls to spare.Athapaththu's all-round display earned her the Player of the Match award after contributing both with the bat and ball in the series decider. Harshitha Samarawickrama, meanwhile, was named Player of the Series after scoring 173 runs across three matches while being dismissed only once.The victory marked a significant milestone for Sri Lanka Women's cricket, ending a 24-year wait for an ODI series win over Pakistan and showcasing the team's growing consistency in the 50-over format.The two sides will now shift their attention to the three-match T20I series, which begins on July 31 in Dambulla.
Article Summary: Sri Lanka Women beat Pakistan Women 2-1 in ODI series decider at Hambantota. Victory is Sri Lanka's first bilateral series win over Pakistan since 2002. Hosts chased down record target of 274 with eight wickets in hand. Harshitha Samarawickrama named Player of the Series.

Article Title: 'They still have plenty to offer': 'Asian Bradman' Zaheer Abbas backs Virat Kohli, Rohit Sharma for 2027 World Cup
Article Text:
India's Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli (ANI Photo)

'Experience makes the difference'

Rohit's century leaves Zaheer impressed

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan captain Zaheer Abbas has thrown his weight behind Indian batting icons Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma , insisting that both veterans still have plenty left in the tank and should be part of India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup.The legendary Pakistan batter, popularly known as the 'Asian Bradman', dismissed concerns surrounding the duo's age and said their skill, experience and continued ability to score runs make them automatic contenders for the marquee tournament, which will be jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia."Both are very, very good in terms of skill and, given their experience, I don't see any reason why they should not play the World Cup. Age should not be a factor as long as they are fit and continue scoring runs," news agency PTI quoted Zaheer as saying on a Pakistani television channel.Zaheer, regarded as one of Pakistan's finest batters after scoring more than 100 first-class centuries during his illustrious career, believes Kohli and Rohit possess qualities that only grow stronger with time.According to the former Pakistan skipper, scoring runs becomes second nature for players of their calibre after spending years at the highest level, while their experience remains invaluable in major ICC tournaments.He also assessed the fitness of the two Indian greats, saying Kohli continues to maintain exceptional physical standards."Kohli is still supremely fit, while Rohit just needs to pay a little more attention to his fitness," Zaheer observed.The Pakistan great added that India would benefit immensely from having both veterans in the dressing room during the 2027 World Cup campaign.His remarks come at a time when speculation over the future of India's senior stars continues despite both producing match-winning performances in the ODI format.Zaheer reserved special praise for Rohit after watching the former Indian captain's recent century against England, saying the opener's batting remains a delight to watch."I watched Rohit score a hundred against England, and it is still a pleasure to watch him bat. He plays so effortlessly and with such sweet timing," he said.Rohit's knock against England once again underlined his credentials in the 50-over format, while Kohli has also continued to deliver consistently, strengthening the argument that the experienced pair could still play a crucial role at the next World Cup.Reflecting on the changing nature of modern cricket, Zaheer acknowledged that T20 cricket has introduced several innovative strokes into the game. However, he insisted that the fundamentals remain just as important, saying every batter aspiring to succeed across formats must master traditional shots like the cover drive and the cut shot.The former Pakistan captain also spoke about his country's cricketing future, expressing confidence that better days lie ahead."Hopefully, the return of Babar Azam as Test captain will turn things around. He is a world-class player and, once he starts scoring runs consistently again, it will have a positive impact on the rest of the team as well. Good times will return for Pakistan cricket," Zaheer said.
Article Summary: Zaheer Abbas says Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma should be part of India's squad for the 2027 ODI World Cup. The legendary Pakistan batter dismissed concerns surrounding the duo's age. Zaheer said their skill, experience and continued ability to score runs make them automatic contenders for the marquee tournament.

Article Title: Former India U-19 World Cup hero Manjot Kalra stays behind bars after bail denied in Lanka Premier League match-fixing case
Article Text:
File Pic: Manjot Kalra (PTI Photo)

Court rejects medical grounds for bail



Match-fixing allegations widen as more players join complaint



Jaffna Kings ownership terminated amid ongoing investigation



NEW DELHI: Former India Under-19 World Cup-winning star Manjot Kalra will remain in custody in Sri Lanka after a Colombo court rejected his plea for early bail in connection with an alleged match-fixing case linked to the ongoing Lanka Premier League (LPL) 2026.Kalra, who shot to fame with his match-winning century in the 2018 Under-19 World Cup final, and fellow Indian national Yuvraj Pushpa had approached the Colombo Chief Magistrate's Court seeking relief after being remanded until July 31 following their arrests earlier this month. However, Chief Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama dismissed the application, allowing the existing remand order to continue as investigators pursue the high-profile corruption probe.According to PTI, defence counsel K.W.S. Fernando sought the release of both accused on medical grounds, telling the court that Kalra and Pushpa were unwell.The prosecution opposed the plea, arguing that the investigation being carried out by the Sri Lanka Police's Special Investigation Unit (SIU) for the Prevention of Offences Relating to Sports was still in progress. Accepting the prosecution's submissions, the magistrate declined to grant bail, ensuring that both accused remain in custody until at least July 31.The latest ruling marks another setback for Kalra, who has been at the centre of one of the biggest controversies to hit the sixth edition of the Lanka Premier League.The case stems from allegations that attempts were made to influence players participating in LPL 2026 to manipulate matches.Sri Lanka internationals Bhanuka Rajapaksa, Avishka Fernando and Dunith Wellalage initially lodged complaints with investigators. During Monday's hearing, the court was informed that two additional Sri Lankan cricketers had since joined the complaint, taking the total number of players involved in the case to five.Investigators had earlier informed the court that multiple players were allegedly approached with proposals relating to match-fixing. According to submissions made during the initial remand proceedings, the players alerted the Sports Corruption Investigation Unit and continued communicating with the suspects under the investigators' instructions.Authorities have also claimed to possess recorded telephone conversations and video evidence connected to the alleged approaches. However, Kalra's defence has denied all allegations, maintaining that there is no evidence showing he offered or paid any bribe.Following his arrest, Kalra had issued a statement asserting that he was fully cooperating with investigators and remained confident that the facts would establish his innocence.The controversy has also triggered significant developments off the field.Last week, Lanka Premier League commercial rights holder Innovative Production Group (IPG), in consultation with Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC), terminated the franchise agreement with Sports Commune, the ownership group behind Jaffna Kings, citing its failure to fulfil financial obligations.Kalra had become a co-owner of the franchise alongside entrepreneur Mayank Goel. Following the termination, IPG and Sri Lanka Cricket assumed full financial and operational control of the franchise to ensure the tournament continued without disruption.Tournament organisers confirmed that Jaffna Kings would continue under the same name, with no changes to their squad, fixtures or coaching staff. They also reiterated that the ongoing investigation involving Kalra would not affect the conduct of the tournament.The Lanka Premier League 2026, featuring five franchises across 24 matches, began on July 17 and is scheduled to conclude on August 8. While the tournament continues on the field, Kalra's immediate future now hinges on the outcome of the ongoing investigation, with his remand set to continue until July 31.
Article Summary: Manjot Kalra and Yuvraj Pushpa will remain in custody until at least July 31. Former India Under-19 World Cup-winning star is accused of match-fixing. Two more Sri Lankan cricketers join complaint, taking total to five.

Article Title: From idolising Mirabai Chanu to competing against her: Gyaneshwari Yadav's rise continues
Article Text:
Gyaneshwari Yadav

Chhattisgarh has rarely occupied centre stage in Indian sport. Gyaneshwari Yadav believes her own journey has followed a similar path - being overlooked amid lifters from more established weightlifting centres. That is, until Monday thrust her into the spotlight.The 23-year-old announced herself to a wider audience with a career-best total of 199 kg to win silver in the women’s 53 kg category on her Commonwealth Games debut in Glasgow. “Now people will know my name and also that I come from Chhattisgarh, which doesn’t boast of many known athletes,” Gyaneshwari told TOI .“It was a big opportunity for me and I’m glad I won silver. I gave my all for gold, but that was not meant to be. I’m happy for the way I lifted and made my country, my parents and my state proud,” she said.Gyaneshwari is the daughter of Deepak Yadav, a former bodybuilder who now works as an electrician in Rajnandgaon. She began dreaming of a CWG medal after watching the movie ‘Dangal’ with her family soon after switching from powerlifting to weightlifting. “I had just switched to weightlifting from powerlifting and I watched ‘Dangal’ with my family.Me and my dad got so inspired that we decided to work hard, and win medals for the country,” she said.Deepak had once hoped to pursue sport himself but set aside that ambition to support his family. “Since I wanted to pursue sport, my father took us from our village, Bhodiya, to Rajnandgaon, where we lived in one room on my school campus. It has been a struggle for us but I believe it will be worth it if I win medals for my country,” she said.When Gyaneshwari began weightlifting, Mirabai Chanu was her idol. “She still is,” Gyaneshwari said. At Glasgow, however, they competed in different categories: Mirabai won gold in the 48kg. That could change on the road to LA 2028.At Paris 2024, women’s Olympic weightlifting featured five categories — 49kg, 59kg, 71kg, 81kg and +81kg. LA28 will have six — 53kg, 61kg, 69kg, 77kg, 86kg and +86kg. With 48kg absent from the Olympic programme, Mirabai is expected to move up to 53kg, potentially putting Gyaneshwari in direct competition with her idol for selection. “I know it will be a mixed feeling to compete against your idol, but then I would be only showing my respect to her by giving my best against her,” she said.
Article Summary: Gyaneshwari Yadav won silver in the women’s 53 kg category in Glasgow. The 23-year-old announced herself to a wider audience with a career-best total of 199 kg to win silver. She is the daughter of Deepak Yadav, a former bodybuilder who now works as an electrician in Rajnandgaon.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Valluri Ajaya Babu betters father's bronze with a silver
Article Text:
Valluri Ajaya Babu (Image credit: X)

Vizianagaram’s 21-year-old Valluri Ajaya Babu went one better than his father by clinching the silver medal in the men’s 79kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on Monday night.Ajaya Babu’s second-place finish to Malaysia’s Erry Hidayat Muhammad was a display of strength, resilience and composure, and it came exactly 16 years after his father Srinivasa Rao had bagged bronze at the Delhi Commonwealth Games.The young lifter from Andhra Pradesh lifted 149kg in snatch and 181kg in clean and jerk for a total of 330kg — a Games record momentarily. In a contest that swung with every lift, Hidayat had the final say, lifting 184kg in his last clean and jerk attempt to finish with a Games-record total of 331kg, edging the Indian by the smallest of margins. England’s Chris Murray claimed the bronze with a total of 325kg.Ajaya was disappointed not to win gold. “Though I’m a little bit disappointed for missing gold, I am excited to win the silver. Had I avoided a minor mistake in snatch in my second attempt, I could have easily won the gold,” Ajaya told TOI from Glasgow on Tuesday.Nevertheless, the havildar at the 3EME Centre, Bhopal, believes the silver will help his career.“I know this medal will boost my confidence and help me qualify for the Asian Games and LA 2028,” he said.Ajaya Babu entered the clean and jerk phase with confidence after dominating the snatch competition. Despite failing in his second attempt at 149kg, he cleared the weight in his final try, setting a new CWG record and ended the snatch category ahead of Murray (148kg) and Hidayat (147kg).If the snatch showcased his technical brilliance, the clean and jerk highlighted his fighting spirit.When Hidayat lifted 181kg to rewrite the Games record, Ajaya Babu responded immediately by matching the weight and reclaimed the record with a total of 330kg. Hidayat summoned one final effort and lifted 184kg to snatch both the record and the title in a thrilling finish.Ajaya Babu’s silver was India’s sixth weightlifting medal at the Games. The silver medal is the latest chapter in a remarkable rise that has gained momentum over the past two years. At the 2025 Commonwealth weightlifting championships in Ahmedabad, Ajaya Babu won the men’s 79kg title with a personal-best total of 335kg (152kg snatch and 183kg clean and jerk), shattering championship records and securing direct qualification for the 2026 CWG.Ajaya Babu followed in his father’s footsteps after watching him train at the 3EME centre in Bhopal. “I developed love for the sport after watching my father,” said Ajaya.
Article Summary: Vizianagaram’s 21-year-old Valluri Ajaya Babu clinched the silver medal in the men's 79kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow. The young lifter from Andhra Pradesh lifted 149kg in snatch and 181kg in clean and jerk for a total of 330kg.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Gulveer Singh, Harjinder Kaur silver medals add lustre to campaign
Article Text:
Gulveer Singh (Image credit: X)

(WITH INPUTS FROM AGENCIES)

Gulveer Singh won an unprecedented silver for India in the men’s 10,000m in the early hours of Wednesday. He clocked 27:49.78 to finish just behind Australia’s Ky Robinson. Meanwhile, Harjinder Kaur clinched a sensational silver in the women’s 69kg weightlifting event, setting personal bests of 101kg in snatch and 126kg in clean and jerk for a 227kg total. Canada’s Charlotte Simoneau claimed gold with a combined total of 240kg.Jadumani Singh confirmed a third medal of the day from the boxing ring after defeating Zambia’s Mwengo Mwale 5-0 by unanimous decision in the men’s 55kg quarterfinal. Semifinalists are assured of a medal as there are two bronze medals awarded in boxing events.Earlier, Asian Games bronze medallist boxer Preeti Pawar assured India a medal after registering a unanimous-decision win over Northern Ireland’s Nicole Clyde in the women’s 54kg quarterfinal. Bhiwani’s Preeti, 22, registered a 5-0 win and advanced to the semifinals.In the other bout, Asian Champion Priya Ghanghas added one more medal after winning an aggressive bout 4-1 on points against Scotland’s Niamh Mitchell in women’s 60kg quarterfinal.Meanwhile, Parveen Hooda lost her quarterfinals bout 2-3 to England’s Sacha Hickey.Vishal TK advanced to the men’s 400m semifinals after clocking 46.49sec to finish second in his heat.He was the 14th-fastest qualifier overall, with 46.62sec the final cut-off time.On Monday, Sarvesh Kushare lit up the field on a cold, rainy evening in Glasgow by winning a silver in the men’s high jump. He waited long for his turn to come, before finishing with second position at 2.25m.Men’s 110m hurdles national record-holder Tejas Shirse ran the race with a stress fracture in his left foot to finish eighth and last in the final on Monday. Shirse had qualified after clocking 13.76s in the heats to become the first Indian to enter the final at CWG. Running with a taped foot, Shirse finished the race in 15.39s.Valluri Ajaya Babu added a silver in the men’s 79kg weightlifting event with a total of 330kg, missing gold by just 1kg. He lifted a Commonwealth Games-record 149kg in the snatch before managing 181kg in the clean and jerk. Malaysia’s Erry Hidayat Muhammad won gold with a Games-record total of 331kg.Nirupama Devi’s campaign in the women’s 63kg category, however, ended without a total. Her only successful snatch was 93kg on her second attempt, having failed at the same weight in her opener and at 95kg in her third attempt. In the clean and jerk, she failed all three attempts at 123kg and was marked DNF.In the pool, Srihari Nataraj reached the men’s 100m backstroke semifinals after clocking 55.58sec. Sajan Prakash failed to advance to the men’s 50m butterfly semifinals after clocking 24.94sec. In the men’s S13 50m freestyle para-swimming heats, Ravi Budigina and Ali Imam both qualified for the final.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh won an unprecedented silver for India in the men’s 10,000m in Glasgow. Harjinder Kaur clinched a sensational silver in the women's 69kg weightlifting event. Jadumani Singh confirmed a third medal of the day from the boxing ring.

Article Title: Teacher-turned-athlete Shilpa KS overcomes odds to win F57 shot put bronze after dramatic review
Article Text:
Shilpa KS (Image credit: X)

MYSURU: At four, when most children are hopping and skipping around, Shilpa KS lost her left leg in a road accident. Her family could not afford treatment, or even a wheelchair.More than three decades later, the little girl from Kanchugara Koppalu village in KR Nagar taluk completed an extraordinary journey to the Commonwealth podium, winning bronze in the women’s shot put F57 at the Games in Glasgow on Monday.Shilpa produced a personalbest throw of 7.26m. She had initially finished fourth, but the Indian contingent successfully protested against Nigerian Eucharia Iyiazi’s 8.19m effort, which had been declared valid. Following a review, officials ruled the throw a foul, elevating Shilpa to the bronze-medal position.The medal capped a remarkable story of resilience. Born into a farming family, Shilpa grew up unaware that para sport existed. Curious glances and insensitive remarks were part of everyday life, but her parents ensured that she completed her education despite their limited means.Sport entered her life only in 2019. Then working as a Kannada teacher, Shilpa was introduced to para sport by a fellow bus commuter. She initially excelled in sitting volleyball before former India para-volleyball player and coach Raghavendra SG spotted her potential and persuaded her to switch to athletics.The transition demanded immense sacrifice. Shilpa juggled teaching with gruelling training sessions before eventually quitting her job to pursue sport full-time. Under coach SD Eeshan at Bengaluru’s Sree Kanteerava Stadium, she developed into one of India’s promising para throwers.She won silver and bronze at an international meet in Thailand, earned a national shot put medal in Goa and struck gold at the 2025 World Para Athletics Grand Prix in New Delhi. Yet financial challenges persisted. Shilpa continues to train with a basic Jaipur Foot rather than a specialised sports prosthesis.Speaking to TOI , an emotional Shilpa thanked everyone who stood by her. “Years of hard work, dedication and sacrifice have finally paid off,” she said.
Article Summary: Shilpa KS lost her left leg in a road accident when she was four. Her family could not afford treatment, or even a wheelchair. Shilpa produced a personalbest throw of 7.26m. She had initially finished fourth, but the Indian contingent successfully protested against Nigerian Eucharia Iyiazi's 8.19m effort.

Article Title: CWG 2026: Ravi Veera Venkata Bhavan Budigina, Ali Imam miss out on medals in men's 50m freestyle S13 final
Article Text:
Ravi Veera Venkata Bhavan Budigina

NEW DELHI: Indian para swimmers Ravi Veera Venkata Bhavan Budigina and Ali Imam were unable to finish on the podium in the men's 50m freestyle S13 final at the Commonwealth Games 2026. The two swimmers ended their campaign with sixth and eighth-place finishes respectively. The S13 classification is a para-swimming category for athletes with visual impairments.Budigina reached the final after qualifying in sixth position and finished the medal race at the same spot.The Indian swimmer clocked 25.68 seconds in the final but could not break into the medal positions.Ali Imam also maintained his qualifying position in the final. He completed the race in 28.28 seconds to finish eighth overall.Scotland's Stephen Clegg delighted the home crowd by winning the gold medal with a time of 24.73 seconds.South Africa's Nathan Hendricks secured the silver medal after clocking 24.84 seconds, while Canada's Nicolas Guy Turbide took bronze with a timing of 24.96 seconds.
Article Summary: Ravi Veera Venkata Bhavan Budigina and Ali Imam finish sixth and eighth respectively. Scotland's Stephen Clegg won the gold medal in the 50m freestyle S13 final. The S13 classification is a para-swimming category for athletes with visual impairments.

Article Title: 'We are proud of you': Manipur CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh's video call with Mirabai Chanu, Rishikanta Singh after Commonwealth Games medals - WATCH
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Mirabai Chanu and Rishikanta Singh were congratulated by Manipur Chief Minister Khemchand Yumnam after winning medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games. During a virtual interaction, the Chief Minister praised the two weightlifters for bringing glory to both Manipur and the country. Manipur CM interacted virtually with Mirabai Chanu and Rishikanta.Mirabai clinched the gold medal in the women's 48kg category, while Rishikanta won silver in the men's 60kg event in Glasgow.During the video call, the Chief Minister congratulated both athletes and said, "Congratulations to both of you. Thank you very much. Mirabai, you bagged the gold medal, and Rishikanta, you bagged the silver medal! We are proud of you."He further said, "Both of you are a pride of the state. We are very proud and happy that you have brought laurels to the state of Manipur and India. Let's catch up once you come back to Manipur."The Olympic medallist thanked the Chief Minister and expressed gratitude to the people of Manipur and the country for their continued encouragement."Sir, it's all because of your support that we've reached this stage. We have achieved such a feat because of the love, encouragement and appreciation of the people of Manipur and the whole of India.For players like us in this discipline, it's our duty to think only of achieving the goal. Without your love and support, we alone could not have achieved this. Sir, we receive huge support and encouragement, and the credit goes to you and the people of Manipur and India," Mirabai said.Mirabai won gold medal in the women's 48kg category. It was her third consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medal after her victories in 2018 and 2022.She also set new Commonwealth and Games records before lifting 105kg in the clean and jerk to secure the title.Rishikanta also impressed in the men's 60kg category, winning silver with a total lift of 264kg, including 121kg in the snatch and 143kg in the clean and jerk.He created a new Commonwealth Games snatch record with a personal-best lift of 121kg. Malaysia's Mohamad Aniq Kasdan claimed gold with a Games-record total of 273kg, while Kenya's Joshua Mboya won bronze with 260kg.
Article Summary: Mirabai Chanu and Rishikanta Singh congratulated by Manipur Chief Minister Khemchand Yumnam. Chief Minister praised the two weightlifters for bringing glory to both Manipur and the country. Mirabai clinched the gold medal in the women's 48kg category, while Rishkanta won silver in the men's 60kg event in Glasgow.

Article Title: History, silver & semifinals! Gulveer Singh, Harjinder Kaur lead India's strong day 6 at CWG 2026
Article Text:
Gulveer Singh, Harjinder Kaur Win Silver (Image: PTI AND AP)

Gulveer, Harjinder bring home silver



Boxers guarantee three more medals



Jadumani Singh defeated Zambia's Mwengo Mwale in the men's 55kg quarterfinal.

Preeti Pawar outclassed Nicole Clyde of Northern Ireland in the women's 54kg quarterfinal.

Priya Ghanghas overcame Scotland's Niamh Mitchell in the women's 60kg quarterfinal.

Mixed results in athletics and swimming



Weightlifting setback, bowls victory

India's medal tally after July 28

Medal Athlete Sport Gold Mirabai Chanu Weightlifting Gold Sharmila Dhankar Women's Shot Put F57 Silver Rishikanta Singh Weightlifting Silver Muthupandi Raja Weightlifting Silver Gyaneshwari Yadav Weightlifting Silver Sarvesh Kushare Men's High Jump Silver Gulveer Singh Men's 10,000m Silver Harjinder Kaur Weightlifting Silver Valluri Ajaya Babu Weightlifting Bronze Bindyarani Devi Weightlifting Bronze Shilpa K. Shyla Women's Shot Put F57 Bronze Jhandu Kumar Para Powerlifting

India enjoyed another productive day at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow on July 28, adding two silver medals to its tally while its boxers continued their impressive run by assuring three more medals with semifinal berths.Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh and weightlifter Harjinder Kaur headlined India's performances, while mixed fortunes followed across athletics, swimming, para swimming, boxing and lawn bowls.The biggest highlights of the day came from athletics and weightlifting. Gulveer Singh scripted history by becoming the first Indian to win a Commonwealth Games medal in the men's 10,000m, claiming silver with a brilliant time of 27:49.78. He stayed with the leading pack throughout the race before producing a powerful final-lap sprint to finish behind Australia's Ky Robinson.In weightlifting, Harjinder Kaur claimed the silver medal in the women's 69kg category with a total lift of 227kg, improving on the bronze medal she won at the Birmingham Commonwealth Games.India's boxing contingent continued to impress as Jadumani Singh, Preeti Pawar, and Priya Ghanghas all advanced to the semifinals by winning their respective quarterfinal bouts, ensuring at least bronze medals.However, Kapil Pokhariya exited the men's 90kg event after losing to Scotland's Robert McNulty, while Parveen Hooda bowed out following her defeat to England's Sacha Hickey in the women's 65kg quarterfinal.Athletics produced contrasting results for the Indian contingent. Vishal TK booked his place in the men's 400m semifinals, while Rajesh Ramesh failed to progress from the heats. Young high jumper Pooja Singh also saw her campaign end after missing out on a place among the medal winners.In the pool, Srihari Nataraj qualified for the men's 100m backstroke semifinal but could not advance to the final after finishing sixth in his semifinal race. Veteran swimmer Sajan Prakash finished 28th overall in the men's 50m butterfly heats and missed out on a semifinal berth.India also endured disappointment in weightlifting as Nirupama Devi Seram recorded a Did Not Finish (DNF) in the women's 63kg competition after failing to register a successful clean and jerk lift. Meanwhile, the lawn bowls duo of Dinesh Kumar and Navneet Singh kept India's hopes alive with a victory over the Cook Islands in the men's pairs sectional match.
Article Summary: Long-distance runner Gulveer Singh and weightlifter Harjinder Kaur headlined India's performances. Mixed fortunes followed across athletics, swimming, para swimming, boxing and lawn bowls. India endured disappointment in weightlifting as Nirupama Devi Seram recorded a Did Not Finish (DNF)

Article Title: 'TJ told me to move forward': How injured Tejaswin Shankar put aside his heartbreak to help Sarvesh Kushare script CWG history
Article Text:
Sarvesh Kushare and Tejaswin Shankar during the CWG 2026 high jump final in Glasgow.

From medal contender to coach on the sidelines

'It really stings'

Eyes now on decathlon return

NEW DELHI: Tejaswin Shankar's own Commonwealth Games campaign ended in heartbreak, but the Indian high jumper ensured his disappointment did not stop a teammate from making history.The national record holder, forced out of the men's high jump competition by a recurring knee injury, stayed back at the venue to guide compatriot Sarvesh Kushare from the sidelines. The advice proved decisive as Kushare overcame a shaky start to clinch the silver medal — India's best-ever result in the event at the Commonwealth Games.Tejaswin had won a historic bronze at the 2022 Birmingham Games, the country's first medal in Commonwealth Games high jump. On Monday, however, the 27-year-old's title hopes were dashed before they had truly begun.Tejaswin experienced a sharp pain in his knee during the warm-up and was unable to continue after clearing only his opening height.Instead of leaving the arena, he remained beside the competition area, closely watching Kushare's attempts and offering technical inputs that helped the Indian recover after struggling midway through the event.Kushare revealed that Tejaswin's timely advice transformed his competition."I wanted to clear the height in my first attempt itself, but during 2.25m my rhythm was affected and my stride became shorter. Then TJ told me to move forward in my run-up, and that helped," Kushare said after winning silver.The medal improved on Tejaswin's bronze-winning effort from Birmingham and marked India's finest-ever Commonwealth Games finish in men's high jump.A visibly emotional Tejaswin admitted the injury struck at the worst possible moment."I felt a shooting pain in my knee. It happened during my warm-up. It's nothing new; I have always had tendonitis in my knees," he said. "I don't think there is any high jumper who doesn't have it. That's why it's called jumper's knee. Everyone manages it, and so do I."The timing of the flare-up made the disappointment even harder to accept."But it's one of those days. You want just one day in a year when you don't have that pain, but it came on that day only. It really stings. In these conditions, I was really confident I could jump for a win, jump for a medal. I really knew I could win a medal,” he said. "But to not even get through the first height, it stings because I was in really great shape."Explaining the issue further, he added: "It's just overuse of the patellar tendon. There is nothing spectacular about it. It just flared up today and ruined my entire competition."Despite the setback, Tejaswin has not given up on his Commonwealth Games campaign.The versatile athlete remains optimistic of recovering in time for the decathlon, which begins on Thursday."I will come back in two days. We still have two days. I'll give my best over the next two days and try and fix this. I will obviously start. I'm not here on vacation," he said. "The patellar tendon is used in high jump and long jump, so if I'm somehow able to get by those two events, I'm still confident the other events will be fine."Tejaswin is the national record holder in the decathlon too.
Article Summary: Tejaswin Shankar was forced out of the men's high jump competition by a recurring knee injury. Shankar stayed back at the venue to guide compatriot Sarvesh Kushare from the sidelines. The advice proved decisive as Kushare overcame a shaky start to clinch the silver medal.

Article Title: Roberto Mancini returns to rescue Italy after three straight FIFA World Cup misses
Article Text:
Roberto Mancini (AP Photo)

Mancini returns three years after dramatic exit



The man who revived Italy gets another rescue mission







No easy road ahead for Mancini



Roberto Mancini has been handed the daunting task of rebuilding Italy once again, with the former European Championship-winning coach returning to the Azzurri dugout as the four-time world champions look to end their alarming World Cup drought.Italian Football Federation (FIGC) president Giovanni Malagò confirmed Mancini's appointment as Italy's new head coach on Tuesday, while former Italy midfielder Claudio Ranieri has been named the federation's new technical director.The decision comes after a turbulent period for Italian football, with the national team failing to qualify for the last three FIFA World Cups. The crisis deepened after former coach Gennaro Gattuso and FIGC president Gabriele Gravina stepped down in April following Italy's latest qualification failure.Mancini's return marks a surprising comeback almost three years after he left the national team in August 2023. The 61-year-old had guided Italy to European glory in 2021 but resigned unexpectedly before taking charge of Saudi Arabia just two weeks later.Malagò acknowledged Mancini's controversial departure but said all factors had been considered before bringing him back."It is clear that all the necessary assessments have been made," Malagò said when asked about Mancini's exit."I certainly took it into consideration; I am aware of his recent apologies, and obviously, everyone has made the appropriate evaluations."Explaining the decision, the FIGC chief said time was a major factor in choosing Mancini."Time was running out … I believed the person who should become the new coach of Italy is Roberto Mancini, for a whole list of reasons," Malagò said.Mancini and Ranieri are expected to address the media together at their official presentation.Mancini's first stint as Italy coach began in 2018 after the Azzurri suffered the humiliation of missing the World Cup in Russia. He inherited a team searching for identity and transformed it by blending experienced players with emerging talent.Under Mancini, Italy became one of Europe's most attractive teams, producing a remarkable 37-match unbeaten run, a world record at the time.The revival reached its peak at Euro 2020, where Italy defeated England on penalties at Wembley to lift the trophy and restore national pride.However, the World Cup heartbreak returned soon after. Italy suffered a shock 1-0 home defeat against North Macedonia in the 2022 playoff semifinal, missing out on the tournament in Qatar.Despite the setback, Mancini remained in charge before his sudden resignation in 2023. After leaving Saudi Arabia in 2024, he most recently managed Qatar club Al-Sadd before departing last month.Mancini's return comes after Italy explored several options, including Andrea Pirlo, while high-profile names such as Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti were also approached but declined the opportunity. Former Italy coach Antonio Conte was another candidate.The new coach will face an immediate challenge, with Italy scheduled to play Belgium, Turkey and France in the Nations League.Malagò warned that Mancini will have limited time to prepare the team."The new coach will have two training sessions to prepare for the first game," he said.He added that Italy cannot expect an instant transformation against some of Europe's strongest sides.
Article Summary: Roberto Mancini appointed new coach of Italy. Former Manchester City boss returns to Azzurri dugout. Claudio Ranieri named new technical director. Italy have failed to qualify for last three World Cups. Mancino led Italy to European glory in 2021.
